0.1.unit: Cooling Water Tower Ver 1 cools 340 m³/h of circulating water for the process users from 49.2 °C (TI-201) to 32.3 °C (TI-202) at the design weather (wet bulb 27 °C, dry bulb 33 °C), a duty of 6.62 MW. Three induced-draught cells E-201/202/203, each with its fan P-212/213/214, drop the water into the basin T-201. Three of the four circulating pumps P-215…P-218 send it through the supply header (PI-202, FI-202, TI-202) to the users and back through FCV-201 (FIC-201) to the cells. LIC-201 holds the basin level with city-water make-up; AIC-202 blows down on conductivity; acid holds the pH. The users' key cooler outlet TI-203 (≤ 47 °C wanted, 45 °C at design) is what the users feel.

rows.what: Process units: product coolers about 1 °C warmer than this morning
TI-202 supply 33.97 °C against 32.32 °C at design and rising slowly since the start
TI-202 HI alarm first at 00:39:04, clearing and coming back every few seconds (2 times by 00:40)

0.4.ctx: Day shift, early afternoon. The unit was lined out this morning at design and nothing was changed on the cooling water. Three pumps, three fans and all three risers in service; the spare pump P-218 stopped. Normal at design: supply 32.3 °C, return 49.2 °C, circulation 340 m³/h, wet bulb 27 °C, approach 5.3 °C, users' outlet 45.0 °C.

R.1.p: A cooling tower can only cool the water toward the wet-bulb temperature of the air, never below it. Each cell exchanges heat and water vapour with the air drawn through it by the fan; the driving force is the difference between the enthalpy of saturated air at the water temperature and the enthalpy of the air. Two numbers describe the tower: the range (TI-201 − TI-202, set by the users' heat load and the circulation) and the approach (TI-202 − TI-231, set by the tower's capability: fill, distribution, air flow, water per cell). At a higher wet bulb the saturation curve is steeper, so the same tower with the same water and air reaches a smaller approach; a tower that has lost capability shows a LARGER approach at the same weather.

R.2.eq: Q = ṁ·cp·(T_hot − T_cold)    Range = TI-201 − TI-202    Approach = TI-202 − TI-231    KaV/L = ∫ cp·dT / (h_s(T) − h_a)

3.2.n: Approach = TI-202 − TI-231 = 33.97 − 30.02 = 3.95 °C against 5.32 °C at design: SMALLER, as Merkel predicts for a healthy tower at a higher wet bulb. Duty Q = 94.4 kg/s × 4.18 × (50.39 − 33.97) = 6.45 MW against 6.62 MW: the users still give the same heat. Range 16.42 °C ≈ design 16.90: no extra load. The supply is warm because the air is warm and humid, not because the tower is worse.

rows.c: 341 vs 339 m³/h — no loss in between
TI-203 +1.3 °C and TI-201 +1.2 °C — the warmer supply is real

3.5.tree:
TOP: TI-202 1.7 °C above design
 OR — The air is hotter and more humid (wet bulb up)
 OR — The tower lost capability
    OR — Fill fouled / distribution poor (one cell)
    OR — Fan stopped or slow
 OR — Less circulation (pump, FCV-201)
 OR — More heat from the users
 OR — TI-202 reads high
3.5.cut: Single-element cut sets; the approach SMALLER than design prunes the whole “tower lost capability” branch.

3.10.n: Team agrees: judge the tower by its approach to the wet bulb, not by TI-202 alone.

3.11.n: Nothing found in Explore contradicts it

5.1.proof: Wet bulb +3.0 °C with the approach 3.95 °C (smaller than design 5.32); T-1: all cells equal, fans running, local readings agree; T-2: TI-203 46.3 → 44.8 °C with more water
5.1.mech: Hot humid afternoon → wet bulb 27 → 30 °C → the air leaving each cell can take up less heat at the same water temperature → the whole tower settles at a warmer cold-water temperature (TI-202 +1.7 °C) while its approach even shrinks → the users' coolers get warmer water → TI-203 rises about 1.3 °C.

rows.opt: Start the spare pump P-218 and raise FIC-201 to 380 m³/h for the afternoon; back to 340 m³/h with three pumps when the wet bulb falls
Tell the users and let them ride it out (they are still below 47 °C)
Clean the tower / inspect the fans
Weather-compensated limits: alarm on the approach, not on TI-202 alone; review the TI-202 HI setting and deadband

rows.step: Start P-218 (spare), check it runs (PG-218, sound), then raise FIC-201 SP 340 → 380 m³/h
Watch PI-202 (stays below 450 kPa g) and FIC-201 HI; stop at 400 m³/h
When TI-231 is back below 28 °C, FIC-201 back to 340 and P-218 stopped
Ask instruments to review TI-202 HI (34 °C, chattering) — add a deadband or an approach alarm
Tell the process units what we did and what to expect

5.7.n: Users as predicted: TI-203 46.3 → 44.8 °C, margin back to 1165 $/h. TI-202 rose to 34.6 °C as predicted (approach 4.68), which keeps the TI-202 HI alarm (34 °C) standing and costs points on the supply band of the score — expected physics, not a new fault: with 379 m³/h the cells get more water for the same air. Extra power 12 kW. Decision: keep it for the afternoon; the users' TI-203 is what matters.

5.8.rule: When the supply is warm with every fan running, compare the approach (TI-202 − TI-231) with design before blaming the tower: an approach at or below design means the weather, and more circulation helps the users.

6.0.n: T-1 and T-2 behaved as predicted. The tower needed no repair; the users were helped by more circulation. The only surprise was the alarm: a fixed TI-202 limit cannot tell weather from a tower problem.

rows.m: Approach alarm (TI-202 − TI-231 > 6.5 °C) beside the TI-202 HI alarm
TI-202 HI: add a 0.3 °C deadband and a 30 s delay (it chattered every few seconds)
Hot-day SOP: spare pump and FIC-201 up to 380 m³/h when the wet bulb passes 29 °C; back down below 28 °C

6.1.kpi: Approach TI-202 − TI-231, trended daily against the wet bulb — it rises before TI-202 does when the tower really degrades

rows.i: No needless tower cleaning or cell outage
Extra 12 kW of pump power while P-218 runs; TI-202 stays above its 33.5 °C band on hot afternoons

hz.cause: FIC-201 raised too far with four pumps
hz.cons: FCV-201 wide open, PI-202 high, pump run-out
hz.sg: Stop at 400 m³/h (FIC-201 HI); PI-202 below 450 kPa g; design P 600 kPa g

hz.cause: P-218 in use on hot afternoons
hz.cons: A pump trip has no standby
hz.sg: Return to three pumps when the wet bulb falls; watch the auto-start logic

6.3.fut: Every utility whose limit follows the weather needs weather-compensated alarms and a hot-day procedure.

6.4.how: Margin recovered 106 $/h for about 4 h of hot afternoon ≈ USD 426, less 12 kW × 4 h × USD 0.10/kWh ≈ USD 5; a needless tower cleaning (≈ USD 5 000 and a cell outage) avoided (assumed prices).

6.5.again:
Look at the wet bulb and the approach before judging the tower.
Use the field round to tell one cell from the whole tower.
Use a small reversible move (the spare pump) to help the users.
6.5.never:
Never order a tower cleaning because TI-202 is warm on a hot afternoon.
Never trust a fixed TI-202 limit to tell weather from equipment.
